name: _to_dense
description: Representative ATen signature (not an exclusive ABI), copied verbatim: aten::_to_dense(Tensor self, ScalarType? dtype=None, bool? masked_grad=None) -> Tensor. This representative signature does not narrow the contract: the original Gems pytest defines the full contract, i.e. the overloads, keyword arguments, returns, errors, aliasing and mutation that must be supported, and tests must never be removed or the reference behavior adapted to fit this one signature. All supplied registered schema strings, verbatim: aten::_to_dense.out(Tensor self, ScalarType? dtype=None, bool? masked_grad=None, *, Tensor(a!) out) -> Tensor(a!) ; aten::_to_dense(Tensor self, ScalarType? dtype=None, bool? masked_grad=None) -> Tensor. The ATen defaults for dtype and masked_grad are None and are retained here as JSON null, matching the parameter metadata. Semantics derived from the tests: densify a sparse tensor into a dense strided tensor, scattering each stored value at its coordinates and summing colliding stored values for uncoalesced duplicate coordinates (COO, hybrid COO included). Coverage exercised by the tests: COO value ranges and all listed dtypes, rank-0 COO, stored explicit zeros, duplicate accumulation, exact integer and cancellation duplicate families, NaN/Inf special values, hybrid COO with sparse_dim and a materialised or stride-0 broadcast dense tail, hybrid duplicates, CSR/CSC compressed layouts (with and without shared structure), BSR/BSC block layouts including stored zero blocks, strided stored values, explicitly coalesced input, empty storage, masked_grad forward passing, backward to stored values and to the sparse input (which stays sparse), rejection of dense input, of a dtype conversion argument, of a non-ScalarType dtype argument and of a non-bool masked_grad argument, plus rejection of FP8 input only in the NVIDIA-scoped, FP8-capability-gated case that the tests actually collect. The densification tests check the sparse input's layout, its stored parts and, for COO only, its coalesced flag against a pre-call reference copy; the rejection tests take no such reference and assert no input-mutation property. The out= keyword is owned by the out overload: it writes into the caller-provided buffer and returns that same buffer (returns_alias_of itself and mutates it), while the representative default overload's schema declares no aliasing or mutation; conditional/overload-dependent effects are therefore described here rather than modelled. The optional dtype argument requests a conversion the tested float and compressed kernels reject instead of performing.
